issue_context.title: Incomplete interface flags on Linux
issue_context.body:
#4063 changed the way flags are captured for network interfaces on linux. Before, flags would come from `getifaddrs`. With this PR flags are now read from '/sys/class/net/<dev>/flags'.

The problem is that not all flags are exported via `sysfs`, namely `volatile` flags as you can see at https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/uapi/linux/if.h.

We need to either revert to the old method or get this information from somewhere else. At least some information is exported via other files in `sysfs`.
comments: I filed the original bug that started the change to sysfs. The problem with the old way was that it wasn't correctly representing the promiscuous mode set in a common way. If at all possible, let's try to settle on a solution that preserves a way to accurately expose the promiscuous mode.
Hi @fossam thanks for the tip. I'll make sure I don't break that. I think the solution will be to get the missing information from other sources, but I still need to investigate.

review_comments: Please do the same filtering here.
These would need to fetch the flags for both linux and non linux. I dont think it should be filtered otherwise we would have missing flags for non linux.
True, the comment is not in the best place. We should still filter inside the Linux block before ORing the flags from sysfs.
Is there away to do this without preprocessor macros? Can we use the osquery platform functions?

we could use isPlatform(PlatformType::TYPE_LINUX) if we want to just know the os. But here it seems we are using platform specific interfaces for example see headers L19-22 for linux. I think in this case we cant remove the macros.
